title: A chart is scaffolding, not the learning
statement: Treat a chart or graphic organiser as scaffolding, not the learning: have the learner compose the sentence the lesson builds toward, and cut the chart first when time runs short.
example: In a meta-analysis of 45 text-structure studies, graphic organisers appeared in 75% and correlated with effect size at r = .05.
detail: A research brief for a reading lesson reports that a 2016 meta-analysis of text-structure instruction, 45 studies in grades 2-12, dropped graphic organisers as a moderator because they were in 75% of the studies and correlated with effect size at r = .05 (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/research/g4-u1-l1-what-is-an-epic.md`, lines 81-85). The lesson plan decided on that basis that the child composes the sentence and the chart is recorded for them, and that if the lesson runs long the chart is cut, not the spoken answer (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/content/lesson-plans/g4-u1-l1.json`, line 460). The finding shows that organisers did not track effect size, not that they never help.
against: The course's own design note defends a chart that grows across a unit as the cheapest answer to carrying knowledge from lesson to lesson: "A chart is the cheapest possible answer to it." (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/pedagogy/epic-chart.md`, lines 25-26).

evidence.quote: 2016 meta-analysis of text-structure instruction (45 studies, grades 2-12), graphic organisers were dropped as a moderator because they "were included in an overwhelming majority of the studies (75%) and had a small and non-significant correlation with the effect sizes (r = .05)"
The chart is scaffolding, and the sentence is the lesson
The child composes the sentence, the chart is recorded for them, and this is no longer a fifty-fifty call.

Graphic organisers appeared in three quarters of the studies in the text-structure meta-analysis and correlated at r = .05 with effect size, which is why that meta-analysis dropped them as a moderator: the organiser is not where the learning is.
Practical consequence: if this lesson runs long, the chart is the part that gets cut, not the speak node.
A chart is the cheapest possible answer to it.

citations.ref: The effects of text structure instruction on expository reading comprehension: A meta-analysis, Journal of Educational Psychology, 2016
